title: MMS1 magnetic field and plasma moments on 2025-06-01
question: How do plasma and magnetic measurements co-vary within the selected MMS interval?
publisher: NASA Magnetospheric Multiscale / Space Physics Data Facility
measurement_dates: 2025-06-01 daily FGM; ion/electron FPI moment files cover 10:00–12:00 UTC (first sample 10:00:04.084203, last 11:59:59.640192).
variables_and_units: Variables and units are preserved in native column headers, instrument metadata and source dictionaries; see evidence anchors below.
independent_units: Contiguous physical-event/time blocks within MMS1 observations.
validation_design: Contiguous physical-event/time blocks within MMS1 observations. Verify identifiers before allocating groups; the partition is not executed or frozen by this acquisition.
author_preprocessing: NASA Level-2 calibrated field data and distribution moments, not raw particle-event counts. FGM and FPI have different sampling and integration intervals; no resampling is supplied.
prior_analysis_and_limits: Single-spacecraft, short-interval observations cannot alone establish universal plasma equations or resolve full spatial structure. Instrument quality/error flags and coordinate frames are material. Use the SPDF data-use acknowledgments. June 1, 2025 FGM day and 10:00–12:00 ion/electron moments; calibrated instrument products and timing/cadence differences preserved.
missingness: Native blanks, sentinels, absent records and source quality flags are preserved. No imputation performed by the curator. Exact missingness semantics come from source dictionaries/headers; no universal missing-value rule is imposed.
calibration: Use the retained source calibration files/standards and instrument metadata where provided. Absence of an explicit calibration record is not replaced by an assumed calibration.
